# `silk/bench/record`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

The data of a benchmark run: the result file with every raw sample, and the report with the
statistics a renderer draws.

## When to use
Read a [`RunResult`](#RunResult) to work with the raw samples of a run, such as to compare two saved
runs. Read a [`Report`](#Report) to draw a run in a renderer of your own: every number a table or a
chart needs is already in it, so a renderer does no statistics.

## Details
Both types are `silk.schema.schema.Schema` types, written as JSON with
`silk.schema.json.SchemaJson`. `silk.bench.bench` writes the result as
`build/bench/<suite>-<time>.json`, and the report wherever a suite declares an output with
`silk.bench.suite.Format.Report`.

Times are nanoseconds and memory is bytes. A raw sample holds whole numbers; the statistics
of a report are `f64`. Dates are RFC 3339 text in UTC, such as `2026-11-19T14:03:22Z`.

A run never drops a sample. A warm-up run is kept with `warmup` set, and a run whose program
failed is kept with its exit status. A report counts the failed runs of a row in `failures`
and leaves both kinds out of its statistics.

## Examples
```silk
import silk.bench.record { Report }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.schema.issue { SchemaError }
import silk.schema.json { SchemaJson }

// The fastest median of the first benchmark of a report, in nanoseconds.
effect fn fastest(text: &[u8]) -> f64 ! SchemaError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  let report = run SchemaJson.decode<Report>(text)
  let rows = report.benchmarks.asSlice()[0].rows.asSlice()
  let mut best = rows[0].median
  let mut at: usize = 1
  while at < rows.length {
    if rows[at].median < best {
      best = rows[at].median
    }
    at = at + 1
  }
  return best
}

// Text that is not a report is an error, never a guess.
effect fn check() -> i32 ! SchemaError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  let best = run fastest(b"{}")
  if best > 0.0 {
    return 1
  }
  return 2
}

effect fn failed(error: SchemaError | OutOfMemoryError) -> i32 {
  drop error
  return 0
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  return run Effect.catchAll(check(), failed) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
}
```

Import as `Report` with `import silk.bench.record { Report }`.
